$description: The Founder's Foyer — color tokens. Direction: The Speculative. W3C DTCG format ($value/$type) — loads directly into Style Dictionary v4+, Tokens Studio, or any DTCG-aware tool. CSS emission lives in palette.css; keep the two in sync.

ground.$description: Page background — parchment, warm but cool. The page of a lab notebook.

$extensions.foyer.usage: html, body, page surfaces, default card background

ink.$description: Primary text and structural strokes — off-black, never pure black.

$extensions.foyer.usage: body copy, borders, icons, headings, dark surfaces

ink-soft.$description: Secondary text on LIGHT surfaces only — fails AA on ink (3.5:1) and for small text on quiet (3.4:1).

$extensions.foyer.usage: timestamps, footnotes, section labels, metadata — on ground only

signal.$description: Circuit-green, bright — the brand accent ON DARK SURFACES. 9.4:1 on ink. Decorative-only on light surfaces (1.7:1 on ground). For the same job on light surfaces, use signal-deep.

$extensions.foyer.usage: links, cursors, focus rings, episode numbers — on ink or neutral-700+ only; decorative shapes and large icons on light

signal-deep.$description: Circuit-green, deep — the brand accent ON LIGHT SURFACES. 4.7:1 on ground (body AA). The two greens are one idea rendered for two surfaces; never use the bright one for text on light.

$extensions.foyer.usage: links, labels, code text, focus rings, cursor accents on ground/quiet; filled CTA background with ground text (4.7:1)

cobalt.$description: Second accent — inline notation, footnote markers, citation chrome. 6.1:1 on ground, 4.6:1 on quiet. Never on dark (2.6:1 on ink).

$extensions.foyer.usage: em-style emphasis, footnote markers, blockquote rules, hyperlink underline color on ground

rose.$description: Warm counter — softens the cool palette, used sparingly. Decorative on light (2.8:1 on ground); text-safe on ink (5.7:1).

$extensions.foyer.usage: tags (with ink text), warm-context labels on dark, photographic tints — never body text on ground

quiet.$description: Supporting tone — surfaces that recede from ground. Identical to neutral-200 by design; it sits on the scale.

$extensions.foyer.usage: card backgrounds, dividers, hover backgrounds, code blocks, secondary text on ink (11.9:1)

neutral.$description: Warm at the light end (parchment-derived), cool at the dark end (ink-derived). The temperature crossover sits between 400 and 500, smoothed through near-neutral steps so no seam shows in a ramp. Use 300-400 sparingly; the system favors high contrast.
